items.title: Lithuania will provide Ukraine with essential energy equipment – Zelenskyy
items.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Lithuania has agreed to provide essential energy equipment following talks with President Gitanas Nausėda, as Ukraine prepares for further Russian strikes on its infrastructure.

items.title: Prosecutors seeking to return Pochaiv Lavra complex to state ownership
items.teaser: Prosecutors in Ukraine’s Ternopil region have filed a lawsuit seeking to terminate a 2003 agreement granting the Pochaiv Holy Dormition Lavra complex for free use for more than 50 years and return the property to state ownership.

items.title: Russia attacks Kyiv with ballistic missiles hours after peace talks end
items.teaser: Attacks against the capital are ongoing, and details about precise targets are not yet available.

items.title: NATO says only Ukraine has the right to decide fate of its territories
items.teaser: NATO's Deputy Supreme Allied Commander Europe John Stringer has praised Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil infrastructure facilities and questioned the Kremlin's intentions in peace talks, stressing that territorial decisions belong to Ukrainians.

items.title: Russia's largest oil refinery slammed by drones in 8-hour attack 2,500 km from Ukraine
items.teaser: The Omsk oil refinery, a Gazprom facility in Siberia, has a processing capacity of over 21 million metric tons of crude per year.

items.title: Ukraine's intelligence exposes Russian agents of influence in EU countries
items.teaser: The Defense Intelligence of Ukraine (DIU), in cooperation with the Center for Countering Disinformation (CCD), has published information on Russian agents of influence in European Union countries.

items.title: 1,600 Russians died capturing, then retreating from, one small settlement
items.teaser: A hacked database indicates 1,600 Russian troops died in one tiny village in northern Donetsk. Zelena Dolyna is a bloody symbol of the whole wider war.

items.title: 'Ukraine's future is within the European Union' — Irish PM aims to open all EU negotiation clusters for Kyiv by end of year
items.teaser: "We have opened three negotiating clusters and will do all that we can to ensure that the remaining two are opened before the end of the presidency," Ireland's Prime Minister Micheal Martin said on Nov. 11 alongside President Zelensky.

items.title: Zelenskyy on negotiations: There is currently a "window of opportunity" to achieve results before 2027
items.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says political changes expected in Europe and already taking place in the US create an opportunity for a breakthrough in negotiations, while ceasefire proposals remain under discussion.

items.title: Zelenskyy: Americans are trying to find "modifications" to Donbas proposals to end war
items.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Washington is considering different approaches to resolving the territorial dispute over Donbas, but insists that sensitive issues must be settled at leaders’ level.

items.title: Schläger neben Priestern: Polens Präsident marschiert mit radikalen Nationalisten - und brüskiert Tusk
items.teaser: Vier Tage nach dem Anschlag von Krakau ziehen Zehntausende Nationalisten durch Warschau. Die Veranstalter sprechen von mehr als 700.000 Teilnehmern. Premier Tusk lädt den Präsidenten zur Versöhnung ein, doch dessen Palast winkt ab.

items.title: Zelenskyy outlines expectations for meeting with Trump's envoys following their visit to Putin
items.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expects Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to bring Russia's responses on prisoner exchanges, security guarantees and possible ceasefires to their meeting in Dublin on 12 November.

items.title: Russian strikes burn almost six months’ worth of cancer drug for Ukraine — now Kyiv is rethinking how it stores medicine
items.teaser: After months of Russian attacks on warehouses, the state drug buyer is shipping stock out to hospitals and regional depots.

items.title: Russia recruits 45,959 foreigners to fight against Ukraine — but doesn’t take a single one back from captivity, Kyiv says
items.teaser: Russia has pulled fighters from 151 countries into its war on Ukraine.

items.title: Ukraine war latest: 'Large-scale' prisoner exchange agreed as 2nd day of Abu Dhabi talks concludes, Umerov says
items.teaser: Key developments on Nov. 11: 'Large-scale' prisoner exchange agreed as 2nd day of Abu Dhabi talks concludes, Umerov says Zelensky reveals when Ukraine expects first delivery of Swedish Gripen fighter jets Russia strikes 6 major power substations, causing outages across Ukraine Hackers target Ukraine's state news

items.title: Ukraine captures first Indonesian prisoner of war as Russia steps up foreign recruitment
items.teaser: The man, originally from the Indonesian island of Java, was sent to participate in a Russian assault in southern Ukraine. After his unit came under a Ukrainian drone attack, he managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory, where he was taken prisoner, according to the I Want to Live project.

items.title: Bloomberg: Over 11,000 foreign nationals killed fighting for Russia in Ukraine
items.teaser: Hacked data from Rosstat reveals that Moscow has registered thousands of war-related deaths of nationals from nearly 100 countries since the start of the full-scale invasion.

items.title: Woman, 68, sentenced for donation to Ukrainian military hospitalised in Russia: "She's barely able to stand"
items.teaser: A 68-year-old woman from Zaporizhzhia Oblast, serving a sentence in Russia over a purported donation to the Ukrainian Armed Forces, requires urgent care following severe weight loss.

items.title: Ship tonnage and gun caliber no longer define sea power, Ukraine’s former commander-in-chief tells forum aboard British carrier
items.teaser: Naval warfare stands at its biggest transformation since the invention of the torpedo.

items.title: Zelensky arrives in Dublin for European Political Community summit, expects a debrief from Witkoff, Kushner
items.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky added that a meeting with U.S. special envoys — Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner — will also take place in Ireland, following the envoys' trip to Russia.

items.title: How we got here: 5 years of the Kyiv Independent
items.teaser: The Kyiv Independent history began in November 2021. Founded by a small group of journalists in a coworking space in Kyiv and a single newsletter, "Ukraine Daily." This November, the Kyiv Independent, Ukraine's leading English-language media outlet, turns five.

items.title: Zelenskyy and his team arrive in Ireland
items.teaser: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy has landed in Dublin with his team to participate in the 9th EPC Summit and hold talks with US envoys.

items.title: Hackers target Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform, replace website with anti-Ukrainian messages
items.teaser: The hackers replaced the agency's homepage with the word ZELENET, an image of a crossed-out Ukrainian flag, and a link to a Telegram channel. Ukrinform's account on X was also renamed ZELENET, while its biography was changed to include a pro-Russian slogan.

items.title: Kremlin says Putin will meet Witkoff and Kushner on 12 November
items.teaser: US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will hold talks with the Russian leader in Moscow following the trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Ambassadors of EU member states approve new Russia sanctions: 50 banks listed
items.teaser: The Committee of Permanent Representatives has provisionally approved the addition of 145 individuals and legal entities to the European Union's sanctions lists over Russian aggression.

items.title: Russland und Ukraine vereinbaren Gefangenenaustausch
items.teaser: Bei den Ukraine-Gesprächen haben Moskau und Kiew einen weiteren Gefangenenaustausch vereinbart. Morgen wollen die US-Gesandten Kushner und Witkoff zu Kremlchef Putin reisen. Dabei soll es auch darum gehen, die Europäer in die Gespräche einzubinden.

items.title: Russian strike on market in Chornomorsk kills four, injures nine – photos
items.teaser: Russian forces struck a market in central Chornomorsk, Odesa Oblast, with a jet-powered drone, killing four people and injuring nine others.

items.title: What do front-line units pick most from Ukraine’s unique 1,800-item weapons store? They have already ordered over $2 billion there
items.teaser: In-stock items now arrive in about eight days.

items.title: Old Khata's 'Kvitky' — Tribute to beauty and enduring legacy of Ukrainian folk art
items.teaser: Imagine your family has survived World War I, a nationwide revolution marked by brutal violence and constantly changing governments, and a famine. Then, less than a decade later, another, even more devastating famine strikes your land under its new rulers. You and the people around you have suffered for years,

items.title: Ukraine's Security Service hits Russian missile ship Naro-Fominsk
items.teaser: Ukrainian Security Service drone operators have hit a cruise missile carrier during a night-time operation targeting oil and port infrastructure in Leningrad Oblast.

items.title: Ukrainian parliament passes EU-linked prosecution reform bill slammed by anti-graft experts
items.teaser: Anti-corruption activists and legal experts have lambasted the recent prosecution reform bill because it does not envisage the participation of any independent or international experts. Prosecutors will dominate in all the bodies supposed to reform the prosecution service.

items.title: Bundeskabinett beschließt Aufbau einer Gasreserve
items.teaser: Mit einer nationalen Gasreserve will die Bundesregierung die Versorgung in Krisensituationen sichern - dabei geht es ausdrücklich nicht um hohe Preise, sondern um Ausnahmefälle wie etwa Sabotage. Auf die Gaskunden kommen dadurch Mehrkosten zu.

items.title: Winter is Russia's weapon
items.teaser: It is astonishing how the most modern and technologically advanced war on the planet ultimately depends on nature. Every drone, from the smallest to the largest, is first and foremost a bird, subject to the laws of aerodynamics and the wind.

items.title: Russian ambassador to Washington dies at 66
items.teaser: Alexander Darchiev, Russia's ambassador to the U.S., died unexpectedly at the age of 66, Russia's Foreign Ministry announced on Nov. 11, without commenting on the cause of death.

items.title: Warum die Ukraine-Friedensgespräche kaum vorankommen
items.teaser: Nach dem zweitägigen Treffen zwischen der Ukraine und Russland unter der Vermittlung der USA sind die Differenzen nach wie vor groß. Ein Überblick über die Ergebnisse.

items.title: Freight transport costs in Russia soar by 30% due to fuel crisis
items.teaser: The ongoing fuel shortages in Russia have led to a significant increase in logistics costs. Road haulage rates have risen by nearly a third, potentially pushing up food prices.

items.title: German government assesses possibility of contact between Merz and Putin
items.teaser: Berlin acknowledges a growing chance of direct communication between the German chancellor and the Russian leader following the recent trilateral negotiations on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Russia strikes 6 major power substations, causing outages across Ukraine
items.teaser: Substations were hit in Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, Zhytomyr and Cherkasy oblasts. Power lines were also damaged in Kirovohrad and Rivne oblasts, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said.

items.title: Florian Kellermann, ARD Kiew, zu den Gesprächen zwischen Russland und der Ukraine in Abu Dhabi
items.teaser: Florian Kellermann, ARD Kiew, zu den Gesprächen zwischen Russland und der Ukraine in Abu Dhabi

items.title: Helsing launches European alternative to Palantir’s military AI
items.teaser: German defense technology company Helsing on Nov. 11 unveiled Clarity, a military AI platform pitched as a sovereign European alternative to U.S. providers such as Palantir, promising military control over their data, AI models and operations.

items.title: Russian drones attack Kyiv Oblast: one killed, several injured, kindergartens damaged
items.teaser: Russian drones hit Yahotyn in the Boryspil district in Kyiv Oblast, killing one person, injuring others and damaging two kindergartens, homes and a car.

items.title: Russia's largest oil refinery hit by drones 2,500 km from Ukraine – videos
items.teaser: Explosions have rocked a major Siberian crude processing facility, prompting local authorities to restrict mobile communications and halt airport operations.

items.title: Only one-third of Ukraine’s key transformers are protected from Russian strikes — but biggest threat may be inside system, lawmaker says
items.teaser: Only a third of the main transformers at Ukrenergo’s 84 substations sit in concrete sarcophagi.

items.title: Kommentar: Russland sägt an der europäischen Sicherheitsarchitektur
items.teaser: Bei den Verhandlungen in Abu Dhabi geht es längst nicht nur um die Ukraine, meint Stephan Laack. Russlands Forderungen zielten auch in Richtung der europäischen Sicherheitsarchitektur. Deshalb müssten alle Alarmglocken schrillen.

items.title: Russia proposes new security system involving non-aggression pacts with NATO countries – Reuters
items.teaser: Russian officials have outlined new ideas for Europe's security architecture, suggesting bilateral non-aggression agreements with NATO countries

items.title: Russia claimed in Abu Dhabi to hold Donbas land Ukraine controls, and the US confirmed Kyiv’s picture, Zelenskyy says
items.teaser: Day two ended with a large prisoner exchange agreed, Arakhamia says. US envoys go to Putin in Moscow next, then to Zelenskyy in Dublin.

items.title: 'Large-scale' prisoner exchange agreed as 2nd day of Abu Dhabi talks concludes, Umerov says
items.teaser: The exchange was also confirmed by Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, who is leading Russia's delegation.

items.title: Russia retook positions Ukraine spent nearly a year clearing during Oleshky truce, Kherson regional head says
items.teaser: Russia brought Grad launchers in during the Oleshky truce, Prokudin says, and 34 more left-bank villages are as critical as the town.

items.title: Crossed-out flag and pro-Russian slogan: hackers attack state news agency Ukrinform
items.teaser: Hackers replaced the agency’s homepage and added a pro-Russian slogan to its X profile. Ukrinform is working with the SSU and cybersecurity authorities to restore its services.

items.title: Trump's son-in-law urges Europe to appoint single representative for talks with Russia
items.teaser: Trump’s envoy Jared Kushner says the appointment of a single representative would help Europe coordinate its position on Ukraine and post-war security in negotiations with Russia.

items.title: “This will be the Kremlin’s sixteenth deadline”: What does Ukrainian brigade that hit 57,000 Russian targets think of fresh peace talks?
items.teaser: Ukraine’s negotiating hand is dealt on the battlefield, not at the table, says Yurii Fedorenko, commander of the 429th Achilles Brigade.

items.title: Russian forces strike energy infrastructure facility in Korosten
items.teaser: A Russian drone struck an energy infrastructure facility in Korosten, Zhytomyr region.

items.title: Kharkiv under Russian attack all day: two killed, five injured – photos
items.teaser: Russian forces have been striking the Saltivskyi, Osnovianskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts in Kharkiv on 11 November. Two people have been killed and five injured.

items.title: Successful Neptune, Flamingo, and Storm Shadow strikes doubled this fall, OSINT count shows
items.teaser: Moscow also claims it shot down four US-made Rusty Dagger missiles on 10 November.

items.teaser: The faces of the men Ivan trained come to him in his dreams. They melt and turn into skulls in the mud. Their bodies broken by mortar rounds, they call to him — "save me." In the middle of the night, Ivan gets up from his bed. Anastasia,

items.title: Four injured in Russian drone attack on Poltava Oblast
items.teaser: Four people have been injured, one seriously, when a Russian drone struck an infrastructure facility in the Karlivka hromada A hromada is an administrative unit designating a village, several villages, or a town, and their adjacent territories , Poltava Oblast, on 11 November.

items.title: Poland nears swap of MiG-29s its army can’t use for Ukrainian counter-drone know-how
items.teaser: Warsaw’s offer has shrunk from up to nine jets to two, and Poland is weighing selling some of the rest, above all to Bulgaria.

items.title: Ukraine’s most unusual counteroffensive: foreign volunteers crawl 15 km through ice-cold pipe in gas masks, past Russian corpses to rout the rest
items.teaser: More than 100 Russians were killed and more than 30 captured in the operation, Khartiia said.

items.title: Zelenskyy to meet Trump envoys in Dublin: We will coordinate positions and determine next steps
items.teaser: The Ukrainian president says he will coordinate positions with Trump’s envoys after their talks in Russia, with a new prisoner exchange among the issues discussed in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Russian FPV drone strike on Zaporizhzhia leaves three injured
items.teaser: Russian forces have once again attacked Zaporizhzhia with an FPV drone, leaving three people injured.

items.title: Russian drone attacks on Kharkiv leaves five injured
items.teaser: Five people were injured and several fires broke out in Kharkiv as a result of Russian drone attacks on November 11.
